summary: Supply the total mass of compound, the mass percentage and the mass of solvent and the Mass percent calculator solves for mass of chemical. That makes it useful for a bench calculation involving amounts, concentrations or reaction ratios. Editing anything puts the results away until the next press of Calculate — change one value at a time and the updated answer tells you what that value was worth.

sections.title: How does the Mass percent calculator work?
sections.html:
The Mass percent calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports mass of chemical in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case; then you type in the total mass of compound, the mass percentage, the mass of solvent and the mass percentage (2).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Mass percent calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Mass of chemical=(1 ÷ 100) × mass percentage × total mass of compound
Mass of solute=(1 ÷ 100) × mass percentage × mass of solution
Mass of solute=mass of solution − mass of solvent

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Take I want to find set to mass percentage for a solute, Total mass of compound = 10 g, Mass percentage = 10 and Increment by = 1. The calculator returns Mass of chemical = 1 g.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Mass of chemical = 1 g should be roughly the size you expected from I want to find set to mass percentage for a solute and Total mass of compound = 10 g.

Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Mass percent calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing a solution and checking the numbers first
  • Converting between the units a protocol and your bench equipment use
  • Working through a stoichiometry problem
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the total mass of compound, the mass percentage and the mass of solvent — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Mass percent calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns mass of chemical, derived from the total mass of compound, the mass percentage and the mass of solvent. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Mass percent calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the total mass of compound, the mass percentage and the mass of solvent, which is 12 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter mass of chemical in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Mass of chemical opens in grams and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Mass of chemical = 1 g. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Mass percent calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
